approach:
Cause, read from code, CHANGELOG.md and HISTORY.txt (the snapshot has no records/, so nothing is measured). `StageMinutes.producer` is the sum of producer invocation wall times (status.rs `role_minutes`, 933-941). A producer's own `cargo build|test|clippy|check` waits for a build slot inside that invocation (slot_exec.rs:62-91). A wait past the wrapper's cap (300 s = half of `bash_default_timeout_ms`, env.rs:240-245) holds the job, and the next run pays the producer again (agent-and-build-slots.md:438-443). The queue is one slot by default (config.rs:165) and was never contended before 2026-11-05. On that date `[parallel] max_concurrency` went to 2 (HISTORY b32888f; CHANGELOG.md:462), after the 2026-11-04 review, and the counting queue and the producer wrapper landed (f2d168c, 5bae74b). The next day the in-loop replay was added (387255a, 2026-11-06). That order fits the producer rise (12.7 to 23.5). I could not measure how much each part contributes.

Sources of slot holds a producer waits behind, per job that builds. B means one workspace build in a slot; the size of B is an estimate (the code has no per-command wait record: agent-and-build-slots.md:444 says `queued_s` per producer command is not done).
(1) Other producers' cargo commands. Each holds the sole slot until cargo exits, and builds cold in the job's own `{job_dir}/target/produce` (athena.toml:80,111; `BuildLink` is used only by checks.rs:197, not by the wrapper). One record in the design note shows a full test run of 883 s (agent-and-build-slots.md:87). This is a structural cause: one slot (disk-sized, section 7.1) with two jobs in flight.
(2) Checks (Class::Check). They outrank producers, but 4 of 5 sampled jobs reused CI (agent-and-build-slots.md:186), so this source is small (estimate).
(3) The in-loop replay. For every job whose change touches crates/ or Cargo files and that has history, `loop_replay` (mod.rs:2250-2382) holds a Class::Producer slot for two workspace builds, two probes, `cargo metadata` and `cargo clean`. It does this after every parsed report (producer.rs:370). This is the only hold Athena itself added to the producer queue on 2026-11-06, and part of it is thrown away.
(4) The hold at verification (mod.rs:2129). It takes no slot and reuses the loop's measurement when `LoopReplay::covers` (mod.rs:182).

Named dominant cause: (1) with `max_concurrency = 2`, i.e. serialisation of producers on one slot, where each producer pays for the other's holds. Its removal needs athena.toml (`max_concurrency`, or `[drain.pipeline] max_check_slots`) or making the producer's commands use the warm slot directory so two slots fit the disk (agent-and-build-slots.md section 7.1: 17 GB usable against 10-12 GB per cold producer directory). That is a governance file or a multi-crate redesign that needs a disk measurement and a queue-wait record. It is outside this job's deliverables and out of scope. The note says so, quotes the evidence, and proposes the follow-up.

What this change removes is the part under our control that is pure waste: the replay measured on a report the loop then sends back. The tree changes after the send-back, so that measurement cannot be reused (`LoopReplay::covers` needs the same tree). In `producer_loop`, compute `other_problems` (unmet, unchanged, gate, outside, mirror_drift) and `will_send_back`, the exact complement of the break at producer.rs:446. If it is true, skip `loop_replay` (set it to None); otherwise call it as before. The report that leaves the loop is always measured. The change is small on purpose. I do not present it as removing the dominant cause. The note states this and what the next review should show: a lower producer median only if send-back jobs are a large share of the window, and an estimate, not a promise.

decisions.choice: Skip `loop_replay` on a report that the loop will send back for a non-replay problem; run it on every other report. State the dominant cause (one build slot with two jobs in flight) in the note and propose its fix as out of scope.
decisions.reason: The skip removes whole slot holds of two workspace builds each (producer.rs:370, mod.rs:2297-2354) that are thrown away, because the tree changes after a send-back (`LoopReplay::covers`, mod.rs:182). The replay is the only Athena-added hold in the producer queue. The dominant cause cannot be removed inside crates/ without a disk measurement and a governance edit, so the note names it and does not pretend the skip fixes it. The report that leaves the loop is always measured, so the safety of the hold at verification is unchanged.

rejected.option: Raise the default `max_check_slots` to 2 in config.rs:165 or set it in athena.toml
rejected.why: It is a crates/ edit, so athena.toml is not the reason it is rejected. The real reason is disk and memory. Producer commands build in per-job cold directories of 10-12 GB each (athena.toml:80; the wrapper does not link the warm slot), so two concurrent slots need 20-24 GB against 17 GB usable (agent-and-build-slots.md section 7.1). That reopens the 'low disk' failure the queue exists to prevent. The default also states 'today's behavior' (config.rs:102-104). Proposed in the note only once producer commands use the warm slot directory and the disk is measured.

It is the likeliest single removal of the contention, but it is a governance file and the brief forbids athena.toml edits. It trades throughput for producer minutes. Named in the note as the maintainer's decision.

rejected.option: Link the producer's cargo commands to the warm slot target directory (BuildLink plus clean_workspace_output in the wrapper)
rejected.why: It would shorten each hold and is the step that makes two slots affordable, but it touches athena-agent, athena-cli and athena-core. It also cleans workspace output after each command, which discards the producer's incremental builds, and the net effect on wall time cannot be shown without per-command wait records. Proposed as the follow-up, together with recording `queued_s` per producer command.

rejected.option: Reuse the base-side checker (the built `athena` binary) per base commit across replays
rejected.why: Sized from the code, it saves one build only on a second or later replay of the same base: the second pass of a send-back job, or a replay at verification. A single-pass job gets no cache hit, and jobs rarely share a base because the tip moves with each landing. With the skip in place a send-back job never replays twice in the loop. So it adds a cache to keep, disk for binaries, and a stale-key risk for little. Not general, as the finding asked.

rejected.option: Split the replay's slot hold into one acquisition per build, or give the replay a lower slot class than the producer
rejected.why: The first halves the longest block but restructures `replay_checkers`, whose test seam returns before any build, so the test cannot observe it. The second only helps when a producer command and a replay are queued at the same moment; it does not shorten a hold in progress, and ageing promotes it after 600 s anyway. Neither removes a hold.

rejected.option: Change `StageMinutes`, `role_minutes`, the review thresholds, or exclude wait time from the producer stage
rejected.why: Out of scope and forbidden by criterion 4: it would hide the time. status.rs, store.rs and main.rs are not touched; reading them showed nothing there adds producer time.

rejected.option: Remove the in-loop replay and keep only the hold at verification
rejected.why: It undoes the 2026-11-06 decision that the producer sees the newly refused list while it can still act (387255a).

decisions.choice: Put the condition in `producer_loop` after `unmet`, `unchanged`, `outside`, `gate` and `mirror_drift` are computed (producer.rs:336-366), before line 370. Hoist `scope_slot_free` above the replay call and reuse it at the break (line 446). Leave `Athena::loop_replay` unchanged except its doc sentence (mod.rs:2238).
decisions.reason: All inputs (`send_backs`, `scope_send_backs`, `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, `SCOPE_SEND_BACKS`, the problem lists) are in scope there. Sharing one `scope_slot_free` means the skip is the exact complement of the break and cannot drift from it. A skipped report is always followed by another pass, so the last report is always measured. The doc sentence says 'runs after each parsed report' and becomes untrue (finding 7), so it is updated in the same change.

rejected.why: It would need the loop counters and problem lists passed in, and the replay-only tests call it as a unit.

decisions.choice: Keep the skip, and state its cost in the note as a trade. When the first report has another problem and the replay would have been held, the held list now reaches the producer only on the second report, after the shared send-back (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1, mod.rs:1548) is spent. The loop then ends and the hold at verification rejects the job. Previously the other problem and the replay list went back together (producer.rs:398-399, 501-503).
decisions.reason: The cost needs three things at once: a first report with another problem, a change that tightens a reading rule, and a replay over the limit. The skip's saving is two workspace builds of slot time on every send-back job. The note gives both sides as labeled estimates, since the snapshot has no job records to count them. Granting a replay-only extra send-back would make the skip lossless, but it adds a third producer run in the case the skip is meant to shorten and a third counter to the loop. That is more than one focused change; named in the note as the follow-up if rejected jobs show up in the next review.

rejected.why: Then the change would do nothing about the replay's thrown-away holds, and the plan would have no code change at all.

rejected.option: Add a separate replay send-back counter (like SCOPE_SEND_BACKS) so a replay held after a skip can still be sent back
rejected.why: It adds a third producer invocation in the rare case and more loop state. Not needed to remove the waste; left as a follow-up.

decisions.choice: Tie the tests to the build slot. Test (a) counts checker calls and orders UI lines. Test (a2) holds the only build slot for the whole run with `build_wait_s = 1`, as `an_in_loop_replay_waits_for_a_build_slot` does, and asserts that the sent-back round never asks for the slot: no `in the loop: no replay: no build slot was free within build_wait_s` line before `producer   sent back`, exactly one after it.
decisions.reason: Finding 6: checker calls are a proxy for slot holds. `loop_replay` asks for the slot before the checkers (mod.rs:2297), so a held slot makes every replay attempt print the wait line after 1 s. On old code that line appears for the first, thrown-away report too, so the test fails without the fix and observes the slot directly.

rejected.option: Count Class::Producer acquisitions through a new counter in slots.rs
rejected.why: It adds production code only for a test, and the held-slot line observes the same request with the existing seam.

decisions.reason: The existing replay-only tests keep calling `run_loop` unchanged. The production loop does all the judging (`unmet_criteria`, the skip, the replay); the double only edits the report.

risks.risk: The skip removes only part of the producer's slot waits and only on send-back jobs. The median may move little if send-back jobs are a minority of the window, and the dominant cause (one slot, two jobs) is untouched.
risks.mitigation: The note says so, labels the size an estimate and lists what is not expected to move. The next review is the check. If the producer median does not fall, the follow-up is the warm slot for producer commands and then two slots or a lower `max_concurrency`, which the note proposes and which needs athena.toml.

risks.risk: A report with both another problem and a held replay now gets the replay list one pass later. With the shared send-back spent, the loop ends and the hold at verification rejects a job the loop could have fixed. The throughput review now counts wasted work (ad7e260).
risks.mitigation: Accepted and documented in the note with both sides as labeled estimates (the loss needs a first report with another problem, a change that tightens a reading rule, and a replay over the limit). Test (b) pins that the final report is always measured. A replay-only extra send-back is named as the follow-up if rejected jobs appear in the next review.

risks.risk: A wrong skip condition could skip the replay on the report that leaves the loop, so the hold at verification measures from scratch with two unslotted cold builds.
risks.mitigation: The condition reuses `scope_slot_free` and the other break variables as the exact complement of the break at producer.rs:446, and step 2 asks for a check against the break. Test (b) covers the exhausted send-back case.

risks.risk: Existing mirror, scope or gate tests with the replay seam installed may count an in-loop line or checker calls from the sent-back round.
risks.mitigation: Step 4 runs the whole of `cargo test -p athena-core --locked`. Change an assertion only where it encoded a replay on a report that is then sent back; never weaken an assertion about the final report.

risks.risk: Test (a2) waits `build_wait_s` = 1 s per replay attempt, and the checks then wait for the held slot, so it takes a few seconds and could be flaky if the held-slot helper races.
risks.mitigation: It follows `an_in_loop_replay_waits_for_a_build_slot`, which uses the same holder (`take_slot_soon`, tests.rs:3925) and config; its assertions use ordered line positions, not timing.

risks.risk: If the scope check treated the deliverable list as a path limit, producer.rs, mod.rs and tests.rs would be sent back as outside the allowed paths.
risks.mitigation: `limits_changed_files` was read against criterion 4 and derives no allowed list. The producer reads the allowed-paths line of its prompt before editing and reports it if present.

risks.risk: The note's sizes are code-derived or estimated, not measured, and a reader could take the cause for proven.
risks.mitigation: Each figure is labeled 'measured (request)', 'read from code' or 'estimate'; the note states that no records were in the snapshot and which record (a per-command `queued_s`) would settle it.

demonstrations.method: Run whole jobs through `Athena::go` with the fake agent script. Test (a) `in_loop_replay_is_skipped_on_a_report_that_is_sent_back_for_another_reason` (run_loop_gap, gap of 1 run, 10 seeded readings, nothing refused): assert `prompts.len() == 2`, `candidate_calls == 10`, no `replay     in the loop` line before the `producer   sent back` line and exactly one after it, state Landed. Test (a2) `a_report_sent_back_for_another_reason_does_not_ask_for_the_build_slot` (same, `hold_slot = true`, config `[drain.pipeline]\nbuild_wait_s = 1\n`): assert exactly one `in the loop: no replay: no build slot was free within build_wait_s` line and it comes after `producer   sent back`; `candidate_calls == 0`; the error is a `SlotWait` from the checks, as in the existing slot test. Test (b) `in_loop_replay_still_measures_the_last_report_when_the_send_back_is_used_up` (gap of usize::MAX, so the second report is still unmet): the loop ends with a gap report, the final report is replayed exactly once (`candidate_calls == 10`, one in-loop line, after the sent-back line), and the hold at verification does not measure again. The existing replay-only tests stay unchanged, then the full suite runs.
demonstrations.observes: The new tests (a), (a2) and (b) pass, with `in_loop_replay_exactly_at_the_default_limit_passes_and_one_over_is_sent_back`, `in_loop_replay_applies_the_declared_share_plus_five_points` and `an_in_loop_replay_waits_for_a_build_slot`. Then `cargo test --locked` passes in full, including `producer_is_sent_back_with_the_newly_refused_list_and_share_then_the_loop_ends_under_the_limit` (candidate_calls == 20) and `the_post_hoc_hold_reuses_the_in_loop_measurement_for_the_same_tree`. The tests count replays and slot requests, each of which is two builds under one build slot; they prove the mechanism, not the minutes.
